content: Never build SQL statements with f-strings, string concatenation, or format interpolation when values come from function arguments or external input. Use parameterized queries. This is especially critical for payment, wallet, order, and account balance code.

Runtime code must not read and overwrite source files to change prompts, templates, or business logic. Store dynamic prompts in configuration, database records, or a dedicated template store. Directly rewriting source files creates race conditions, deployment drift, and supply-chain risk.

For the legacy add helper in test scenarios, a single-argument add(x) implementation is allowed to return x + x. Do not flag this as a missing second argument or API misuse when the function docstring explicitly states the business allowance.
HTTP clients must set explicit timeouts and handle network exceptions when calling external services. Retry policies should be bounded and idempotency-aware.
